data.narrative:
Voya Energy is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Richard Wang, Matt Horton, and Steven Kaye, having raised $13M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a climate and energy sector peer set of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Linzia, ticker LNZA), though direct peer multiples at the Seed stage proved insufficiently populated for a robust median-based approach.

Given limited narrow-stage comparables, stage-progression methodology was the primary applicable lens. Using total capital raised ($13M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied value of $32M. This single-method result anchors the analysis; applying ±15% sensitivity bounds produces a triangulated range of $28M (low) to $37M (high), with $32M as the median.

The valuation range of $28M–$37M carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method. Sensitivity to stage-progression assumptions—particularly the applicable step-up multiplier and timing to Series A—represents the chief risk to this estimate. Future validation would benefit from either (i) execution milestones that narrow Series A positioning, or (ii) emergence of more granular Seed-stage comps within climate-tech. The peer universe (Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen) suggests robust sector activity but does not yet provide tight comparable anchoring at this stage and scale.
